sources.entry: Gingko - Tree-structured markdown editor for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

summary.one_liner: Gingko Writer is a tree-structured writing app for organizing and drafting long, complex documents such as novels, screenplays, legal briefs and theses.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Gingko Writer as software for organizing and drafting complex documents, from novels and screenplays to legal briefs and graduate theses. It is a ground-up rewrite of GingkoApp.com, and the README says the latest version is online at gingkowriter.com. The repo holds both halves of the web app: a client/ folder with an Elm and JavaScript frontend bundled with webpack, and a server/ folder with a TypeScript/Express backend. A data/ folder holds local database files that are created on first run. The README also mentions translation contributions and points to client/CONTRIBUTING.md for code contributions.
use_cases: organize a novel or screenplay outline
draft a legal brief in sections
run a local self-hosted writing app for development
contribute to a tree-structured writing tool
how_to_run: Install Node.js 24, Bun, SQLite, Redis and CouchDB (CouchDB admin credentials needed)
git clone git@github.com:gingko/client.git gingko && cd gingko
cd server && npm i && cp config-example.js config.js
Edit server/config.js with your CouchDB admin username and password, then run: npm run build && npm start
cd client && bun i && cp config-example.js config.js
In client/, run: bun run newwatch, then open the local address it serves
notable: Split frontend (Elm) and backend (TypeScript/Express) in one repo
Migration from CouchDB to SQLite is in progress, per the README
Playwright end-to-end tests and Jest server tests
caveats: Setup needs several services: Node.js, Bun, SQLite, Redis and CouchDB
CouchDB is a temporary dependency that will be removed once user documents move to SQLite
The README says installation of the prerequisites varies by system and is not covered
